_doc: The estate's liveness contract. Every capability declares what it must PRODUCE and how
often. A capability with no declared observable is UNPROVEN — a finding, not a pass.
Why this file exists (measured 2026-08-05):
- meta/ESTATE_PAUSED was set 2026-08-02T18:56 and the estate did nothing for 3d 4.5h
while verify_estate.sh reported 'coordinator last_tick 15s ago' and the morning brief
ran daily. Every light was green.
- 21 of 25 enabled cron jobs had no declarable output, so 'did it work' was unanswerable.
- daily-strategist-audit errored once, auto-disabled, dead 7d. otto-dispatch off 46d.
- pull_project_work skipped every project with an empty objective queue, 3d, silently.
None of those were FAILURES. They were SILENCES, and nothing in the estate detects silence.
observable kinds:
file       — newest mtime across `path` (glob ok) proves production
sqlite     — `query` must return one epoch-seconds column; newest row proves production
json_field — glob `path`, keep only records matching `where`, then take the newest.
Filters on CONTENT before freshness. Use it whenever a file being
written does not by itself mean anything happened.
receipt    — measured production from cron/scheduler.py::_write_receipt, which
records the files each job run touched. `requires: artifacts` means a
run only counts if it wrote a non-log file; `requires: exit0` is the
weaker bar, correct only for jobs whose output leaves the filesystem
(a Telegram message). Every exit0 row says so in its note.
none       — NOT DECLARED. Audits as UNPROVEN. Declare it; never delete the row.
The distinction the whole file turns on: a cron last_run_at proves a job RAN. It never
proves it DID anything. That is the signal that read green through the three-day outage,
and it is why no verdict here is allowed to derive from it.

capabilities.what: File one next-move task per active project — the estate working on the founder's products

observable.query: SELECT MAX(created_at) FROM tasks WHERE source LIKE 'project:%'

capabilities.note: This is the capability whose 3-day silence started the 2026-08-05 audit.

capabilities.what: The read-only product research each next-move task is supposed to write
Drift detection between declared and actual estate state
Curate the pending digest the dispatcher reads
capabilities.note: Was kind:file on queue/pending-digest.json until 2026-08-06. That file is CONSUMED by the dispatcher (otto-dispatch.py:164, os.replace -> .processed), so it is legitimately absent between a dispatch tick and the curator's next write. Two audit runs five minutes apart read PRODUCING then DARK with nothing actually wrong — a false DARK on the estate's own alert chain, delivered hourly. The curator's receipt is the honest observable: it records that the curator ran and wrote, independent of whether the consumer has since eaten the file.

capabilities.what: Daily strategy audit across the portfolio
capabilities.note: script field is null and the job was auto-disabled after RuntimeError: Connection error.

capabilities.what: The RSI loop must CLOSE gaps, not merely count them
capabilities.note: The observable is an auto-generated policy that reached status=active — a gap CLOSED, not a gap noted. Measured 2026-08-05: 13 pol-auto policies exist, all provisional, none ever promoted; every active policy on the estate is hand-written. idle-consolidation.py:213 says auto-promotion 'needs human approval' and no channel ever asks, so the learning loop is structurally incapable of applying what it learns. pol-auto-fix-cron sits at hits=9 helped=7 hurt=0 against PROMOTE_MIN_HITS=3.

capabilities.what: Tasks actually reaching a terminal state — the estate finishing work

observable.query: SELECT MAX(completed_at) FROM tasks WHERE status='done'

capabilities.note: Last run 17:19 exited 1 with API Error: Unable to connect to API (ENOTFOUND). The 23:19 run did not fire.
Real output is a Telegram panel; nothing is written to disk, so a clean exit is the strongest available evidence. Upgrade to an artifact bar once sends are journalled.
Two jobs (midday, prebrief) share this script; a receipt from either satisfies it.

capabilities.what: Idle-time continuous learning into the corpus

observable.requires_note: improvement-probe.sh:18 appends to probe-findings.jsonl ONLY when the gateway is down. Producing nothing is its healthy state (48d quiet = 48d of gateway uptime), so requiring artifacts would mark it DARK exactly when it is working. exit0 is the correct proof.

capabilities.what: Repo health check across the estate

observable.requires_note: Observed 2026-08-06: a full run appends only to logs/alerts/watchdog.jsonl, which _scan_produced counts as log_count, not artifact_count. requires=artifacts could therefore never be satisfied by a healthy run.

capabilities.note: Never fired since being enabled; a receipt is the first thing that will prove it ever runs.
Never fired since being enabled. Output is a Telegram probe, so exit0 is the bar.
A clean run with nothing to commit is a legitimate no-op, so artifacts cannot be the bar.

capabilities.what: Watch for uncommitted work across repos
capabilities.note: Reports a clean tree as a legitimate no-op.
A healthy daemon means nothing to write.

capabilities.what: Escalation actually reaches the founder (not merely gets produced)
capabilities.note: Every other capability here measures PRODUCTION. None measured DELIVERY, which is the link that actually failed: otto-dispatch sat disabled 46 days while everything upstream produced correctly and 1,519 alerts went nowhere. The canary rides the real relay (cron tick -> no_agent stdout -> _deliver_result -> telegram) and confirms the PREVIOUS run's arrival by reading last_delivery_error off its own job record (cron/jobs.py:978), so it never trusts its own report of success. Note the circularity this cannot escape: if delivery is broken, the alarm about delivery cannot be delivered either. The non-circular check is the pull-side ALERTS section of verify_estate.sh, which reads state/delivery_proof.json by hand.

latches.what: CEO kill-switch. Blocks the ENTIRE tick before any work is admitted.
latches.note: Set 2026-08-02T18:56, still set 3d 4.5h later. No event row, no audit line, no owner, no reason recorded — set_estate_paused writes an 18-byte file and nothing else. The estate cannot tell you who paused it.
latches.release_policy: NOT auto-releasable, deliberately: a kill-switch that clears itself is not a kill-switch. It escalates every run until a human resolves it — which is exactly the behaviour that was missing for 3.2 days.

latches.what: Cron jobs switched off. A disabled job reports last_status='ok' — it looks healthy because it is not failing, it is simply not running.
latches.note: otto-dispatch off since 2026-06-20 (46d), otto-improvement-pulse since 2026-06-21, daily-strategist-audit auto-disabled 2026-07-29.
latches.release_policy: NOT auto-releasable: re-enabling a job the founder switched off deliberately would change estate behaviour without being asked, and daily-strategist-audit would simply re-fail (its script field is null). Escalates instead, so a 46-day silence surfaces on day one.

latches.what: Breakers left open. A breaker with no cooldown is a latch, not a breaker.
latches.release_policy: Auto-releasable. A breaker is supposed to have a cooldown; one that stays open until a human notices is a latch wearing a breaker's name. Re-opens immediately if the underlying fault is still there, which is the correct behaviour.

latches.what: Enabled jobs that have never run. last_run_at=None means there is NO status at all — the absence a failure-watcher cannot see.
latches.release_policy: Cannot be released — an enabled job that never fired needs diagnosis, not a switch flip. Escalates so the absence becomes a visible failure.
